introduction.en: Poverty estimation in India has evolved from a purely nutritional-based approach to a more comprehensive multidimensional framework to capture the complexity of deprivation.
introduction.hi: Poverty estimation in India has evolved from a purely nutritional-based approach to a more comprehensive multidimensional framework to capture the complexity of deprivation.

body.en: Early committees like Alagh and Lakdawala focused on calorie intake as the primary proxy for poverty. However, the Tendulkar Committee shifted the focus to a uniform consumption basket, acknowledging that poverty is not just about food. The Rangarajan Committee further refined this by including separate baskets for food and non-food items. The current shift towards the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) reflects the understanding that poverty involves deprivations in health, education, and standard of living, which income alone cannot capture.

conclusion.en: A multidimensional approach is essential for targeted policy interventions, ensuring that poverty eradication strategies address the root causes rather than just income deficits.

overview.title: Poverty In India
overview.definition: Poverty in India is defined as a condition where individuals lack the financial resources and essentials for a minimum standard of living, historically measured through caloric intake thresholds and currently via multi-dimensional deprivations.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Crucial for GS Paper III (Inclusive Growth, Poverty, Development) and Prelims (Economic and Social Development - committees, MPI indices, welfare schemes).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Poverty In India.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Absolute Poverty**: Measured by a fixed poverty line based on the minimum cost of living required for basic needs (food, shelter, clothing).
• **Relative Poverty**: Compares individuals' income or consumption against the broader population, reflecting income inequality rather than outright deprivation.
• **Multidimensional Poverty**: Developed by UNDP and OPHI, assessing poverty across health, education, and standard of living indicators simultaneously.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Headcount Ratio (HCR), poverty gap, and squared poverty gap (Foster-Greer-Thorbecke indices).

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: First time defined poverty line based on daily calorie intake (2100 kcal for urban, 2400 kcal for rural).
Nutritional approach focusing on minimum survival needs.

items.definition: Published by NITI Aayog (utilizing Oxford/UNDP methodology), tracking 12 indicators across health, education, and standard of living.
MRP uses 365-day recall for low-frequency items and 30-day for others; MMRP uses 7-day recall for specific food items to capture consumption better.
The goods and services used to calculate the cost of living for the poverty line, including food, fuel, light, rent, clothing, education, and medical care.
Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), National Food Security Act (NFSA), PM-KISAN, and NITI Aayog's National MPI Reports.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Region / Zone Details**: Higher concentration of multidimensional poverty in central and eastern states like Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, and Uttar Pradesh.
• **Driving Advantages**: Urban centers and southern states (Kerala, Goa, Tamil Nadu) show significantly lower HCR due to better human capital, service sector growth, and land reforms.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Informal labor market vulnerability, climate shocks affecting agriculture, and educational gaps.
• **Policy Interventions**: Universal Basic Income debates, formalization of labor, direct benefit transfers (DBT) via JAM Trinity (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile), and asset creation.

items.title: Mnemonic for Poverty Estimation Committees
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'ALL-TR' (Alagh, Lakdawala, Tendulkar, Rangarajan).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Chronological order of major official poverty committees in India (1979 -> 1993 -> 2009 -> 2014).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly solves chronological arrangement questions in Prelims.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Rural calorie norm is always HIGHER (2400 kcal) than urban (2100 kcal) due to higher physical labor intensity.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that the Tendulkar Committee abolished the concept of calorie intake. Correction: It did not abolish calories; it shifted away from using calorie consumption *alone* as the sole metric, including health and education expenditure in the consumption basket.

Mains Value Addition: In Mains, argue that poverty is not merely a lack of income but a deprivation of capabilities (Amartya Sen's Capability Approach). Quote NITI Aayog's National MPI data showing rapid decline in multidimensional poverty to substantiate inclusive growth.

keyTakeaways: Poverty estimation in India has evolved from a pure nutritional/calorie-based approach to a comprehensive consumption-expenditure basket and now to multidimensional deprivation indices.
Spatial disparities remain stark, with northern and eastern states showing higher incidence compared to southern and western states.
Interventions like the JAM trinity and NFSA focus on structural safety nets, shifting the policy paradigm from relief to capability building.
